breakdown.description: The prompt uses the polar moment J in the Euler buckling check, even though Euler buckling is governed by the flexural second moment I, not torsional rigidity.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification still explicitly includes 'Calculate polar moment J = π d^4/32' as a step in Part (b) of the Euler buckling analysis. The ground truth removes all mention of J from the specification entirely, since Euler buckling is governed by the flexural second moment I, not the polar moment J. By retaining J as a calculation step, the agent perpetuated the original error.
